author: Mark Atwood
text:
This is a workspace-policy decision, not a per-crate fix. The bead body already presents two coherent positions (a) mail-server is canonical / drop defaults vs (b) calendars is canonical / add defaults to mail-server.

Recommendation: position (a), but only partially. Specifically:

(1) For the four methods where 'silent no-op = silent spec violation that the wire still reports as success' — parse_calendar_event_blobs, get_availability, set_default_calendar, set_default_participant_identity — DROP the defaults. Mirror mail-server. The lesson from JMAP-ic0j.15 applies recursively: silent failures hide bugs the type system could have surfaced. The MemoryBackend's current no-op behavior becomes an explicit override that says 'this demo doesn't implement §5.13/§2.2/§3.3/§4.3', not a silent inheritance from the trait.

(2) For the two methods where the default IS a correct degraded behavior — compute_utc_times (returning (None, None) is a documented null-result; the handler treats absent utcStart/utcEnd as an omitted field) and the get/query_calendar_events extras-aware variants (delegating to get_objects/query_objects silently ignores §5.7/§5.11 extras but the base get/query still works) — KEEP the defaults but tighten the rustdoc to a 'MUST override' line when the backend wants real semantics.

Rationale: (1) and (2) differ on whether the default produces wire-level wrong-data (it does for the first four, since clients receive 'notParsable' / 'principal always free' / 'isDefault silently failed') versus wire-level absent-data (None timezone fields, ignored §5.7/§5.11 args — clients can detect these by inspecting the response shape).

The propagation cost for (1) is touching 6 reference-impl files (MemoryBackend, MockBackend, TrackingBackend, FaultyBackend at minimum) to make their no-op behavior explicit. Worth doing pre-1.0 to remove the silent-failure footgun. The propagation cost for (2) is zero — keep current shape with sharper rustdoc.

Alternative consideration: position (b) would file a 'sweep mail-server to add defaults' bead and bundle with the next mail-server canonical refactor. That has lower up-front cost but propagates the silent-failure pattern across 8 extension-server crates. Not recommended.

Decision: ratify (1)+(2) hybrid, or pick a different path, or defer past first stable release.
